domains.name: Fundamental principles and concepts of a quality management system (QMS)
Quality management system (QMS) and ISO 9001 requirements

domain_guidance.summary: This domain accounts for 12.5% of the exam and covers core quality management concepts, customer focus, leadership, and process approaches. Candidates learn how these principles guide effective quality management system implementations across organizations.

study_focus: Context of the organization and leadership
domain_guidance.summary: Accounting for 13.75% of the exam weight, this section focuses on specific ISO 9001 requirements. Candidates examine organizational context, leadership commitment, operational planning, support structures, performance evaluation, and continual improvement clauses within standard frameworks.

Weighted at 12.5%, this domain addresses key audit terms, ethical behaviors, and standard principles governing independent reviews. Candidates learn how objectiveness, evidence-based decision making, and professional care apply throughout auditor engagements.

study_focus: Preparing audit plans and work documents
domain_guidance.summary: This domain weighted at 12.5% addresses activities preceding an audit. Candidates study audit scope determination, document reviews, audit plan preparation, resource allocation, and initial team communications required for structured quality evaluations.

Representing the largest section at 22.5%, this domain covers on-site audit execution. Candidates focus on opening meetings, gathering audit evidence through interviews and observations, evaluating conformity, and identifying non-conformities during live assessments.

Carrying a 13.75% exam weight, this section covers closing meetings, report preparation, and follow-up activities. Candidates evaluate corrective action plans, report audit findings to stakeholders, and confirm completion of audit objectives.

study_focus: Managing audit program risks and resources
domain_guidance.summary: Weighted at 12.5%, this domain addresses establishing, implementing, and monitoring audit programs. Candidates review program risk management, auditor competence evaluation, program resource allocation, and continuous audit program improvement strategies.

editorial.exam_day_guidance: Arrive early for your testing session with required identification. Maintain a steady pace to answer all 80 questions, carefully reading each scenario before selecting your response. Focus on applying standard audit principles systematically throughout the exam.

faq.answer_text: The PECB ISO 9001 Lead Auditor Certification exam contains 80 questions in total. Candidates must answer questions covering all quality management and auditing domains to demonstrate their technical knowledge.
faq.question_title: How many questions are on the exam?

faq.answer_text: The passing score for the PECB ISO 9001 Lead Auditor Certification exam is 70%. Candidates who achieve this score or higher demonstrate sufficient mastery of ISO 9001 auditing concepts and program management principles.

Exact exam duration details are provided directly by PECB during candidate registration. Refer to the official PECB documentation or check with PECB directly for specific schedule details and time allotments for your exam session.

The exam covers all exam domains: QMS fundamental principles, ISO 9001 requirements, fundamental audit concepts, audit preparation, audit execution, audit closing, and audit program management, with weights ranging from 12.5% to 22.5%.

editorial.meta_description: Prepare for the PECB ISO 9001 Lead Auditor exam covering QMS principles, ISO 9001 requirements, audit execution, closing, and program management.

methodology.summary: This overview was built using verified official PECB certification guides and standard documentation. Domain weights, topic details, and exam format rules reflect published facts to provide accurate candidate guidance.

editorial.overview: The ISO 9001 Lead Auditor Certification exam, administered by PECB, tests an individual's proficiency in auditing quality management systems. Across all exam domains, candidates face 80 questions that evaluate fundamental quality management concepts, ISO 9001 requirements, audit principles, preparation, execution, closing, and audit program management. Candidates must demonstrate practical mastery of standard compliance and auditing methodologies to earn certification.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Review core ISO quality management principles along with ISO 9001 requirements. Allocate study time according to domain weights, focusing heavily on domain 5, which represents 22.5% of the evaluation. Practice reviewing audit scenarios, defining audit objectives, gathering evidence, and drafting non-conformity reports. Verify your understanding of audit program management and final closing procedures before taking the 80-question exam.
editorial.who_should_take: Quality managers, auditors, consultants, and compliance officers responsible for implementing or evaluating quality management systems should take this exam. It suits professionals aiming to lead third-party or internal ISO 9001 audits and manage organizational quality audit programs.

lifecycle.summary: Confirmed current on the issuer host on 2026-09-19: "If you successfully pass the exam, you can apply for the “PECB Certified ISO 9001 Lead Auditor” credential."
